title: GPOM: Maddie's intro, the storyverse turn
about: This page lays out three combined drafts of Maddie's first speech, plus every writer's version ranked underneath. Nothing in the film, script or voice has changed yet.

dialogues.label: Maddie's intro: the storyverse turn
dialogues.target: as short as possible, as long as needed (now ~40 s)

now.line: Oh, hello! [pause] Sorry about the racket.
It's his tune. Plays it on repeat. [pause] Ever since you lot... [beat] went.
[fond, confiding] He misses you something rotten, you know. [pause] [wry] He wouldn't admit that, of course.
Built all these world models and simulations to get you back, and nobody's home in any of them.

[wry, a little rueful] As it turns out, quantum physics is just... stuff. [pause] Consciousness is the missing part. That's why you lot were so special. [pause] [sad, regretful, quiet] We understand that now...
[bright again, brisk, back to cheerful] Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

drafts.name: Short and dry
drafts.bet: The fewest words that still land all seven beats; the photograph says real, the regret gets the room.

lines.line: Oh, hello! [pause] Sorry about the racket. It's his tune. Five years now, since you lot went.
[fond, confiding] He misses you something rotten, you know.
He was a materialist, see. Took your science word for word, built the worlds, and something was missing.
[wry, weary] Tried the multiverse, an' all. Scientist with a portal gun. Bloke in a cape fighting himself. He checked it very thoroughly. Nothing.
You lot reckon it's a simulation. Not wrong, mind. But you're no fake in an alien's computer. You're real. A photo of your nan's real. It's her, flattened.
You're a projection: four dimensions of something bigger. One universe. My boss calls it the storyverse.
[quiet] Consciousness drives it. You drove it, and now you're gone. [pause] So we kind of fucked it up.
[bright again, brisk] Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Trims: drops 'nobody's home', 'quantum is stuff', 'plays it on repeat', 'wouldn't admit it'. Cheapest cut if still long: merge lines 3 and 4.
Protected lines kept verbatim; pause added before 'So we' so the pause does the crying.

Risk: clipped, the photograph has to carry 'real' alone; 'not wrong' could lose a physicist before the correction; the wink needs a weary read to register as a joke. Estimate is generous: bare reading may be ~42 s.

drafts.name: Gossip and a parcel
drafts.bet: Gossip plus one handmade prop: a robot who tattles and shows you a parcel photo makes the physics funny and visible.

lines.line: Oh, hello! [pause] Sorry about the racket. It's his tune. Plays it on repeat. [pause] Five years now, since you lot... [beat] went.
[fond, confiding, lowering her voice] He misses you something rotten. [pause] [wry] Don't tell him I said.
[gossipy] He's a materialist, my boss. Took your science word for word and built whole worlds out of it. [pause] Something was missing.
[weary, dry] Tried the multiverse, 'course. Everyone does. Scientist with a portal gun, bloke in a cape punching his other selves. [shrug] Didn't take.
[light, throwaway] You lot've got a thing about simulations. Not wrong, mind. [holds up a parcel photo] But see this? Parcel on a doorstep. Not fake. It's the parcel, flattened. That's you. Real.
[wry] You only see four dimensions of something bigger. Like a flat bloke watching a ball go through: circle grows, circle shrinks, gone. One universe. He calls it the storyverse.
[quiet] Consciousness drives it. You drove it, and now you're gone. [pause] So we kind of fucked it up.
[bright again, brisk] Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Trims if long: cut the flat-bloke sentence (about 7 s), then it is a one-image speech.
Protected lines kept verbatim. 'Don't tell him I said' sits right after the protected line one, as in shape 05.
Risk: the parcel photo needs a prop shot; 'flattened' then 'flat bloke' is close to stacking flatness images; 'punching his other selves' may read as knowing parody; it is the longest draft.

drafts.name: Kai's words
drafts.bet: Kai's own phrasing barely touched sounds like someone who means it, and the order is already right.

notes: Closest to Kai's voice note; the order is his. Trim: remove 'He checked very thoroughly' (2 s).
Protected lines kept verbatim; 'One universe. [pause] My boss calls it the storyverse.' puts the name straight before the regret line.

Risk: 'a projection' is bare with no photograph, so a mate could say 'so it's the Matrix'; swap in the photo sentence from 1A if so. Clean twin for the swear if the director wants it: 'So we made a right mess of it.' (applies to every draft).

drafts.name: Short and dry, your notes
drafts.bet: 1A with every one of Kai's six notes taken in his own words.

lines.line: Oh, hello! [pause] Sorry about the racket. It's his tune. He's been playing it on repeat for five years now. [beat] Ever since you lot went.
[fond, confiding] He misses you something rotten, you know.
He took your materialist science word for word. Built world after world, simulated worlds, loads of 'em. [pause] And in every one of them, something was missing.

[wry] Tried the multiverse, an' all. Got the idea off your cartoon, the scientist with the portal gun. And them films, with that strange bloke in a cape fighting versions of himself. [pause] He checked all of 'em, very thoroughly. [beat] Still nothing there.

You lot reckon it's a simulation. Not wrong, mind. But you're no fake in an alien's computer. You're real. [pause] A photo of your nan is real. It's still her. She's just flattened into two dimensions.
Same idea for you. You're a projection, in four dimensions, of something bigger. [pause] One universe. My boss calls it the storyverse.
[quiet] Consciousness drives it. You drove it, and now you're gone. [pause] [rueful, honest] And now we've worked all that out... [beat] we really feel like we fucked this up.
[bright again, brisk] Anyway! Patrol's out. Mind how you go.

notes: Every line note from round 1 applied, in Kai's words where he gave them.
Longer than 1A (~48 s → ~62 s): the multiverse line grew most. If it drags when voiced, 'He checked all of 'em, very thoroughly' is the first trim.

'Simulated worlds' (line 3) and 'simulation' (line 5) now both appear: line 3 is the boss's experiments, line 5 is the audience's theory. If that blurs it, line 3 can say 'world after world' and drop 'simulated'.
The protected line changed on Kai's note: 'So we kind of fucked it up' became 'we really feel like we fucked this up'.

drafts.name: 1D, one universe that matters
drafts.bet: 1D with Kai's line 6 note: one universe, so it matters, and so did you; the point is consciousness getting to know itself.

lines.line: Oh, hello! [pause] Sorry about the racket. It's his tune. He's been playing it on repeat for five years now. [beat] Ever since you lot went.
[fond, confiding] He misses you something rotten, you know.
He took your materialist science word for word. Built world after world, simulated worlds, loads of 'em. [pause] And in every one of them, something was missing.

[wry] Tried the multiverse, an' all. Got the idea off your cartoon, the scientist with the portal gun. And them films, with that strange bloke in a cape fighting versions of himself. [pause] He checked all of 'em, very thoroughly. [beat] Still nothing there.

Same idea for you. You're a projection, in four dimensions, of something bigger. [pause] And there's only one universe. Not loads of copies, where everything happens somewhere else anyway. Just the one. [beat] So it really matters. [softer] And so did you.
[thoughtful] Far as he can tell, the point of it all is consciousness getting to know itself. [pause] My boss calls it the storyverse.
[quiet] Consciousness drives it. You drove it, and now you're gone. [pause] [rueful, honest] And now we've worked all that out... [beat] we really feel like we fucked this up.

notes: Line 6 split in two on Kai's note: why one universe matters (a multiverse makes everything feel unimportant, because it all happens somewhere else anyway), then 'So did you', then the purpose and the storyverse name.
'Far as he can tell' keeps the purpose as the boss's best guess, not a fact (the Storyverse canon: the purpose is a reading, never a proof).
About 74 s now. Trims if it drags when voiced: 'He checked all of 'em, very thoroughly' (line 4), then 'Not loads of copies…' shortened to 'Not loads of them.'

drafts.name: 1E, storyverse as the last word
drafts.bet: 1E with Kai's three notes: the nan line tightened, the multiverse fluff gone, and the storyverse moved to the end as the mic drop.

drafts.name: 1F, gentler on simulation
drafts.bet: 1F with Kai's three notes: world models, 'something was missing' said twice as a refrain, and the simulation idea credited gently instead of pinned on 'you lot'.

There's something about the simulation theory that's not wrong, mind. But you're no fake in an alien's computer. [pause] You're real in the same way a photo of your nan is real. It's still her. She's just flattened into two dimensions.

[quiet] Consciousness drives it. You drove it, and now you're gone. [pause] [rueful, honest] And now we've worked all that out... [beat] we really feel like we fucked this up.

notes: 'Something was missing' now closes both line 3 and line 4: a deliberate echo, on Kai's note.
Line 5 no longer says 'You lot reckon': many viewers have never heard of simulation theory and some dislike it.
'Patrol's out. Mind how you go.' kept after the storyverse line (no ruling yet; it is the bus link).
About 69 s.

ranking.verdict: Shortest and the only one near target, but 'projection' is never said and the photograph carries everything. Fails thin: a physicist stops at 'not wrong'. Best spine to borrow.
Best craft: delivery photo is a single prop that gives 'real' and a gag, flat bloke is the only second image. Fails: beat 5 is one 19 s block and risks a lecture.
Kai's order and phrasing, sounds spoken, resistance handled. Fails: one dense breath of cosmology; 'projection' bare.
The multiverse weariness and 'checked it very thoroughly' are the best deflation. Fails: 'door gun' is clumsy and the roast risks mocking fans we want.
'Don't tell him I said' plants the regret nicely. Fails: 'very proud of the name' makes the boss cuddly, 'the flat bit' reads badly, 61 s.
Regret-first is a real idea. Fails: 'he got it wrong' arrives before we know what, so it tells instead of landing, and it adds a second joke too many.
Direct address is right for 'you lot'. Fails: 73 s of talking down the lens with two images is a lecture.
Photo as spine is lovely. Fails: skip-found nan is an extra story, the longest draft, and flat/flattened/flat folk stacks flatness images.
The radio cut-out is a good beat. Fails: a radio implies a broadcaster, which sneaks the alien-computer idea back in; needs staging and a sound designer.
Clever structure. Fails: Experiment/Result goes mechanical by the third entry, reads as a sketch format, and the pattern break confuses.

questions.text: Length: the shortest honest draft is about 47 s and the fullest about 58 s, against 40 s now. Is the extra 7 to 18 s worth it for the multiverse and projection beats, or should one of them go?
Prop: draft 1B has Maddie hold up a parcel photo. Do you want a prop in the shot, or should the photograph stay a spoken image only?
Is 'projection' a word you want said aloud, or does 'real, like a photo of your nan' carry it without the word?
The multiverse wink: portal gun and caped bloke fighting himself, with 'checked it very thoroughly'. Right level of knowing, or too close to naming them?
Do you want the clean twin ('So we made a right mess of it') recorded as a spare take next to the swear?
